answers.answer: !pause pauses music. Its effective access is moderators, including someone granted the right to moderate the music queue; an ordinary viewer without that right is refused even if the editor’s base role says Everyone. Its default normal chat cooldown is 30 seconds and per-person cooldown is 0 seconds. Platform-identified broadcasters and moderators bypass normal waits, but feature/access checks still apply.
quote: For example, !pause needs a moderator or someone granted the right to moderate the music queue, even though its base role in the editor is Everyone.

For music controls, Moderators includes someone the broadcaster granted the right to moderate the song queue. That gate applies to !pause, !resume, setting !volume, !bansong, !closequeue, !openqueue and !clearsongs. An ordinary viewer without that right receives a refusal.

answers.answer: No. The catalog does not connect a music player; its underlying feature must be configured. The bot must be connected and the command enabled and available. In Commands then System commands, Moderator, Lead moderator, Editor and Broadcaster can normally customize supported fields, subject to a higher requirement set by the broadcaster. Read-only access does not show that tab.
quote: Music and economy commands need their underlying feature configured. Having !pause in the catalog does not connect a music player. To run a command, the bot must be connected and the command enabled and available to the person asking.

To manage a built-in, open Commands, then System commands. By default, Moderator, Lead moderator, Editor and Broadcaster can change commands; the broadcaster can raise the required role. Read-only access does not show this tab.

answers.answer: The Put one field back section says to use Back to default beneath the changed cooldown; it saves immediately and shows Using the default. The full footer Reset to default process is described as losing saved edits, restoring role/cooldowns/replies/read-aloud defaults and switching the command on; shared reply wording also resets. However, another paragraph says Reset to default changes just one cooldown. The article is inconsistent, so the one-field versus whole-command distinction cannot be trusted without resolving that conflict.
quote: Choose Back to default beneath a changed field. It saves immediately, without another Save changes, and the field returns to Using the default.
To return just one changed cooldown to its default, choose Reset to default. This changes only that one field.

A reset loses the command’s saved edits and switches it back on. If it shares replies with another command, the reset also restores that shared wording. The other command keeps its own enabled state, role, cooldowns and Read it aloud setting.

answers.answer: No, normal moderator bypass does not permit the second bare skip five seconds later if the first moderated skip succeeded: music moderators share a separate 30-second window for bare !skip. An ordinary viewer may use !skip 4, subject to normal access checks and having a fourth pending request; it removes that viewer’s fourth pending request counting only their own requests, and leaves the playing song alone.
answers.quote: Bare !skip lets a viewer skip only their own currently playing request. A moderator or music-right holder can skip any playing song, but a successful moderated skip starts a separate 30-second wait for the whole channel. Another moderator cannot skip again five seconds later, even though moderators bypass normal cooldowns. A numbered command such as !skip 4 instead removes the caller’s fourth pending request, counting only their own requests in queue order. It leaves the playing song alone and still requires the command’s normal access checks.

answers.answer: The reset instructions require a consequential reread. One section says Back to default restores one field, then the next explicitly recommends Reset to default for just one cooldown, before saying a reset loses saved edits and re-enables the command. A reader trying to restore one wait could choose the footer action under the false promise that only one field changes, losing unrelated customization or reactivating a command. The bulk consequences are stated before the numbered reset procedure, but they conflict with its immediately preceding one-field promise.
quote: Choose Back to default beneath a changed field. It saves immediately, without another Save changes, and the field returns to Using the default.
To return just one changed cooldown to its default, choose Reset to default. This changes only that one field.
A reset loses the command’s saved edits and switches it back on.

answers.answer: The conflicting spoken labels and scopes for Back to default and Reset to default are materially confusing: a listener hears Reset described as one-field-only immediately before its wider destructive consequences. They must return to the text or another source to avoid losing other settings. The catalog’s length alone is not a material failure.
quote: To return just one changed cooldown to its default, choose Reset to default. This changes only that one field.
A reset loses the command’s saved edits and switches it back on.

findings: A paragraph tells the reader to choose Reset to default for just one cooldown and promises only that field changes. This conflicts with Back to default beneath a field and with the documented whole-command reset that loses saved edits, restores shared wording and switches the command on. Following the one-field promise can cause unrelated configuration loss or unintended reactivation.
